the test found two real bugs. (1) the three scaffold writes live-reloaded the board out from under the compose box before it could show the link — fixed with LiveReload.mute per write, the same fix ext/Ask needed. (2) slugifying the raw ask gave `read-public-framework-ext`, which names nothing: path-ish tokens are now dropped and the compose box grew an optional name field.

assign.outcome:
**You can start work from the browser** — type an ask on `/framework/ai/`, get a task dir and a session working it. No terminal.

- `rpc:start` (`Server/plugins/Start.js`) scaffolds `ai/<date>/<slug>/` — brief + opened log, exactly what the `new-task` skill writes — and spawns `claude -p`.
- **Returns as soon as the process is away, not when the work is done.** A task runs for an hour; its own log is the progress channel and live-reload carries it to the board.
- `--session-id` generated up front, so the transcript is joined from line one.
- `acceptEdits`, not `bypassPermissions`: a web text box should write files, not run anything at all.
- Verified end to end twice in Chromium — Haiku span up, read a file, logged, landed. Kept record: `board-smoke`.
- The test earned its keep: it found the scaffold writes reloading the board out from under the compose box (fixed with `LiveReload.mute`), a slug of `read-public-framework-ext` (path tokens dropped, name field added), and a brief loose enough that both spawned agents wrote malformed `{"log": "string"}` lines (brief now shows the shapes).

Still open: nothing streams the spawned session's progress except its own log lines, so a task that forgets to log looks dead.
